description: We are ASELGET, a group which consists of ASELSAN MTAL students. We are ambigious about our work. We are a game designing community.
summary: In the field of engineering every choice has a major consequence. We have to think about trade-offs and decisions that will affect not only us but every person that we care for. When people's lives are on stake how can we take such decisions in a clear state of mind? Our project does solve this problem. Our challenge was to let people design their space missions and simulate them without actually going to space. We figured out that designing a space mission itself is too complicated to shrink it down just to a sequence of calculations. We had to include human traits and everything that made us think about our decisions and learn something new in a safer way. We have made an interactive simulation game for everyone who sets their eyes to the skies and beyond. They can create, manage and simulate space missions that are being affected by environmental and mechanical factors. They have to think about every aspect of a space mission including financial, social and political terms. We used NASA datasets to make our simulation actually simulate reality rather than being a "space game".
details:
Our project is a real-life interactive space mission design simulation that not only serves a purpose as a simulator, it makes its users experience a "safe pressure" that they have to consider when designing a mission. Creating and designing a space mission is a serious matter that will affect everyone around us. So we figured out that we have to consider every tiny bit of detail for these missions. We have made a simulation that users can manage their space agency, sign new contracts for the parts that they will use for spaceships, create labs and bases in various locations, invest in R&D processes, design their spaceships, assembly their parts, etc. The clear goal is to simulate space missions, achieve some goals, manage a virtual space agency, research new technologies, rise to the top and gain attributes and many more, after all it is designed to be realistic.

However, every decision has an impact on the mission's outcome. Users should think about factors like mass, propellant mass, repulsion, downlink speed, uplink speed, downlink and uplink bottleneck situations, communication, data quality, mission's objectives, starting base, atmospheric conditions and many more. These were the required factors in the challenge's description.

We used Unity as our game engine, pure C# deterministic engine for calculations, webgl and we assembly, CSS for graphic design, our custom UI Toolkit interface rendered in 2D via URP, IL2CPP and Brotli compression for browser deployment, Newtonsoft.Json for JSON catalog loading, xoshiro256 for deterministic simulation, Howard Hinnant's calendar algorithms for date arithmetic, NativeWebSocket for networking, and Unity Test Framework for testing. Version control was handled with Git/GitHub, audio assets were sourced from Kenney and Freesound, Canva and Medibang were utilized for branding and presentations, and OBS Studio alongside DaVinci Resolve powered the video production pipeline. Also SI is used for coding, debugging, information gathering, data analysis, translation. However SI was not a part of thought and creation process, it is a product of human thought process.

As a team we had to think about our missions definition. We have been given a clear definition and set of instructions. Our project shall not be a machine determined simulation. We should let "people" determine the outcomes. Every decision has a consequence, and everyone should think their decisions thoroughly. I think we are creative and different by this. We are not giving people a tool, we are making them a part of the process. So that they can feel like a real human being and experience something real, very real.
